summary_of_change:
Despite market anxiety, Intuit's operational performance demonstrates exceptional underlying resilience. Full-year FY26 revenue reached $21,400.0M (+13.9% YoY), with the latest fourth quarter delivering $4,350.0M at an elite 78.2% gross margin. The business maintains a massive global footprint of 100 million total customers worldwide across Global Business Solutions and Consumer ecosystems (including QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp).

Growth is increasingly anchored by Intuit's 'Big Bets'—Assisted Tax (TurboTax Live), Money, and the Mid-Market Intuit Enterprise Suite (IES)—which grew north of 30% YoY and now comprise a vital portion of total revenue. On the capital allocation front, Intuit generates robust free cash flow, maintaining a clean balance sheet with $3,950.0M in liquid cash against $2,900.0M in total debt ($+1,050M net cash).

Management's strategic shift toward an AI-driven expert platform is expanding monetization beyond basic software subscriptions into transactional take-rates across merchant payment processing, payroll services, and liability-backed expert tax preparation. The mission-critical nature of SMB accounting systems of record creates exceptionally high switching costs and high retention rates across the core ecosystem.

market_pricing_in:
Mr. Market is currently treating Intuit with extreme caution near $278.07, pricing the equity at a compressed 10.3x P/OE. The prevailing narrative assumes that Intuit's double-digit top-line momentum has been largely manufactured through aggressive ARPU price hikes rather than real customer volume expansion, pointing to softening online ecosystem net adds and lower-end DIY tax headwinds from free government tax filing alternatives.

Furthermore, the market views recent workforce restructurings (cutting 17% of roles while absorbing severance and facility realignment charges) as a defensive scramble to offset soaring generative AI compute costs and human-expert support overhead. Instead of valuing Intuit as an elite cash-generative compounder, Mr. Market prices in terminal growth deceleration and margin compression.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: Normalized Owner Earnings stand at $26.98 per share ($7,215.0M total after subtracting $1,450.0M SBC and $175.0M Maintenance CapEx), backed by $+3.93 per share ($+1,050M) in net balance sheet cash.

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: If lower-end DIY tax filers migrate en masse to free government portals, Mailchimp experiences severe churn from low-cost alternatives, and soaring generative AI compute costs disintermediate core software workflows without corresponding ARPU increases, Intuit's top-line model faces structural headwinds.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Total active customer units contract from 100 million down to 92 million over 3 years, while blended monetization yield degrades from $174 to $160 per unit as consumer tax filings compress and merchant payment processing volumes drop.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Because fixed platform investments, AI infrastructure, and compliance expert networks remain sticky at roughly $11,500M in annual cash operating overhead, revenue drops to $14,720.0M ($160 yield × 92M units). Degraded Year 3 Owner Earnings fall to $3,220M ($12.04 per share), shrinking Owner Cash Margin to 21.9%.

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Capitalizing degraded Owner Earnings of $12.04 per share at a conservative trough multiple of 6.5x P/OE (reflecting permanent moat degradation) and adding $2.50 per share in residual net cash yields a Downside Floor Target of $80.76 per share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: Exact starting ecosystem baseline spans 100 million total customers worldwide across Global Business Solutions and Consumer ecosystems (including QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp), producing subscription and transactional take-rates across online ecosystem services, merchant payment processing volume, and tax filing tiers, producing an annualized revenue run-rate of $17,400.0M.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Expanding mid-market adoption (Intuit Enterprise Suite) and global online business ecosystem growth offset DIY consumer tax churn, compounding units at ~3.8% annually: Year 1 = 103 million, Year 2 = 107 million, Year 3 = 112 million active units.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization): Blended monetization yield increases from $174 to $210 per unit as customer mix shifts toward TurboTax Live expert assistance and higher-tier QuickBooks Advanced subscriptions. Projected Year 3 Revenue = 112 million units × $210 yield = $23,520.0M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Cash COGS and operating expenses scale to $14,327M, with stock-based compensation at $1,750M and maintenance CapEx at $220M. Projected Year 3 Owner Earnings = $9,650.0M (Owner Cash Margin = 41.0%, or $36.09 per share on 267.4M diluted shares).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash ($+1,050M) + Cumulative 3Y Owner FCF ($26,250M) - Cumulative Buybacks ($23,000M) - CapEx ($600M) = Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $3,700M ($13.84 per share).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Year 3 Owner Earnings growth rate g₃ = +10.9% YoY ($9,650M vs $8,700M in Year 2). Under the 2-Factor Matrix for Wide Moat Steady Compounding (g₃ between 8% and 15%), an exit multiple of 19.5x P/OE is applied: ($36.09 OE/sh × 19.5x) + $13.84 net cash = $717.60 Intrinsic Fair Value Target, delivering a 37.1% per annum expected IRR over today's $278.07 market price.
